p1200.title: 3000065: proportional factors for bipartite regular cores
p1200.body:
## Accepted restricted result

This authored prose edition proves simultaneous proportional edge
factorization for every finite loopless bipartite multigraph whose connected
components each have empty or regular nonempty 2-core. For arbitrary
positive real fractions summing to one, the same partition satisfies every
color's floor/ceiling quota at every original vertex degree. Core degrees
may vary between components, and arbitrary finite trees may be attached.
Parallel edges, forests, bipartite pseudoforests, isolated vertices, the null
graph, and one color are covered. Irregular surviving 2-cores are outside
the sufficient hypothesis. No mathematical correction was required.

## Complete general proofs

The finite quota-word lemma includes its lower-bound circulation reduction
and integral augmenting-flow proof; it uses the original real fractions.
The complete multiplicity-aware core-structure argument and alternating-path
proof of the perfect-matching decomposition are retained. Monotone prefix
counts extend core colors to attachment edges, and one-precolored-edge
completion propagates through trees. Quotas use original degrees throughout.

The fixed-instance rational-cell lemma preserves both integer threshold
equalities and strict inequalities, including zero-degree and zero/one
unfixed-coordinate cases. It gives no bounded-denominator testing guarantee.
The main theorem treats arbitrary real fractions directly and uses no
finite computation as a premise.

## Authored obstructions and omitted finite premises

A historically checked ten-vertex tree shows that an arbitrary valid first
proportional factor need not extend, even with unrestricted choice of the
remaining colors. The authored local forcing contradiction and its real
parameter region are retained. A historically checked six-cycle point
shows a fractional vertex and non-total-unimodularity of the natural
joint-color LP. The authored odd-cycle determinant and tight-rank arguments
are retained. Both underlying graphs have full valid partitions; neither
obstruction refutes the target.

Explicit graph/factor and coordinate witness packages, indexed rows and
columns, raw matrix certificates, executable code, and raw certificates are
omitted. Realization of each obstruction's stated finite premises is a
historical checked fact, not a self-contained reconstruction in this prose
edition. The general theorem and rational-cell lemma are complete and do
not depend on either obstruction. This is not a computational reproduction
package.

## Historical checks and stream-hash qualification

The independent historical audit checked 15,674 in-scope K3,3 partitions,
4,323 labeled-tree partitions, six retained concrete partitions, both
obstructions, and multiplicity, exact irrational, rational-cell boundary,
endpoint, and negative controls. Normal, -O, and -OO receipts agree.
Candidate programs were not used as implementation source, imported, or
executed by the independent audit.

The candidate's unretained full generated stream hash is authenticated
author-reported metadata only. The audit constructed its own valid
partitions; it did not recreate that stream and claims no byte-identical
reproduction. Edition preparation performed editorial and byte-integrity
checks only, with no new mathematical run or scholarly-source inspection.

## Sources and status

J. R. Correa and M. X. Goemans,
[*Improved bounds on nonblocking 3-stage Clos networks*](https://doi.org/10.1137/060656413),
SIAM Journal on Computing 37(3), 870–894 (2007), Section 2, supplies
two-factor and relaxed-decomposition context. Public author PDF:
https://www.dii.uchile.cl/~jcorrea/papers/Journals/CG2007.pdf .

U. Feige and M. Singh,
[*Edge Coloring and Decompositions of Weighted Graphs*](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-540-87744-8_34),
June 25, 2008 preprint corresponding to ESA 2008, Conjecture 1.4,
Theorem 1.5, and Sections 1.1–1.2 and 3, records the target and contextual
bounds. Public research-site PDF:
https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/wp-content/uploads/2008/09/edgecoloring.pdf .

The retained Egres Open revision 2419,
[*Partitioning a bipartite graph into proportional factors*](https://oldlemon.cs.elte.hu/egres/open/Partitioning_a_bipartite_graph_into_proportional_factors),
is the target formulation, not a current-status certification. The audit's
live opening of that page failed; both public PDFs opened successfully,
without a live PDF byte-identity claim. SOURCES.json distinguishes the
retained hashes and historical passage inspection from those live openings.

The unrestricted same-partition target remains unresolved by this work.
No novelty, priority, exhaustive later-literature survey, or current global
problem-status certification is claimed. This AI-assisted manuscript is
unrefereed. Acceptance means an independent internal AI audit, not external
human peer review, journal acceptance, or formal proof-assistant certification.

Exactly eight authored proof/audit/acceptance/provenance/verification files
are added under unsolved_math_prioritization/attempts/3000065. QUEUE.md and
unrelated paths are unchanged. Copied source bodies, dataset contents,
private sources, private personal data, and private coordination are excluded.

p1201.title: 2398 / EP944: prior vertex-critical resilience results and repaired proof
p1201.body:
## Accepted prior results and exact residual

This authored edition retains the complete repaired proof of Ema Skottová
and Raphael Steiner's 2025 prior result: for every k>=5 and every r>=1,
there exists a finite simple (k,r)-graph. Both appendices, the k=6,8
change-point and two-block bridge, vertex-deletion wraparound, gluing,
sparse critical scaffolds, and all-large-orders allocation are included.
Every correctness-relevant printed repair is explicit. The theorem
statements and parameter thresholds are unchanged. A focused independent
AI audit accepted the repaired proof with no further required correction.

Writing A=8(k-1)(18r+3), the progression orders are n>=A(6r+3)+1 with
n=1 modulo A; every order n>=A[2(k-2)A(6r+3)+2] is covered as well.
These give the square-root subsequence and cube-root all-large-orders
lower bounds for each fixed k>=5. The conventional lower proof is
self-contained and does not import Jensen's theorem or a finite computation.

Separately, two historically executed independent exact searches accept
Alex Chan's graph at commit 697307af42505b11490fdc74c04eda5c7ec76c51:
60 vertices, 180 edges, chromatic number 4, every vertex deletion
3-chromatic, and every single-edge deletion still 4-chromatic.
Its exact three-color defect is 2. It therefore gives k=4,r=1 only;
the family k=4,r>=2 is unresolved by these audited results.

The upper-bound implication separately imports Conlon–Fox Lemma 8.1.
Its source omits the lemma's proof; this edition does not re-prove it.
That dependency is not used in the lower bound.

## Verification and distribution boundary

The finite audit's first exhaustive search uses four verified edge
orbits of sizes 60,60,30,30, with 1230,1464,1207,1219 recursion nodes.
The second uses a distinct complete forward-checking search without
color or graph-orbit quotients: all 181 instances consisting of the graph
and every individual edge deletion were rejected, in 1,651,066 nodes.
Both solvers were checked against exhaustive coloring on 2,198 small-graph
cases each. Sixty graph automorphisms and sixty transported puncture
colorings were explicitly verified. Normal, -O and -OO historical outcomes
agreed. No author code, generated search certificate, or Lean project was
executed. Static Lean-semantic inspection is not formal replay, and the
source's all-k theorem retains its substantive inputs as hypotheses.

Exactly eight authored proof/audit/acceptance/provenance/verification files
are distributed. The complete conventional proof is retained. The finite
result is accepted at the disclosed historical exact-computation boundary;
this prose-only edition is not a computational reproduction package.
Programs, graph/generator/coordinate data, raw colorings and certificates,
copied source documents and images, and private coordination are excluded.
The omitted finite verification inputs and implementations are necessary
to reproduce that computation, but are not premises of the k>=5 proof.
Preparing this edition performed no new mathematical run, scholarly-source
retrieval, visual source inspection, or literature search.

## Attribution and review limits

- Ema Skottová and Raphael Steiner,
  [Critical edge sets in vertex-critical graphs](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.08703v1),
  arXiv:2508.08703v1, 12 August 2025.
- Alex Chan,
  [fixed source repository](https://github.com/alexgocardinal/dirac-critical-graph/tree/697307af42505b11490fdc74c04eda5c7ec76c51).
- David Conlon and Jacob Fox,
  [Bounds for graph regularity and removal lemmas](https://www.its.caltech.edu/~dconlon/RegRem.pdf),
  Lemma 8.1 on printed p. 56 and proof-omission notice on p. 57.
- Paul Erdős,
  [On some aspects of my work with Gabriel Dirac](https://users.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1989-19.pdf),
  printed p. 113, the original k>=4 every-r question.

This AI-assisted work is unrefereed. Acceptance means an internal
independent AI audit, not external human peer review, journal acceptance,
or formal proof-assistant certification. No novelty, priority, exhaustive
global current-literature status, or whole-problem resolution is claimed.

inspection scopes without asserting an updated peer-review status.

p1202.title: 3000088: weighted-coloring proofs for forests and cacti
p1202.body:
## Accepted restricted results

This authored proof/audit edition preserves complete analytical arguments
for weighted edge coloring with arbitrary real weights in [0,1]. The local
parameter b is the maximum optimal unit-bin count at a vertex, not the
ceiling of weighted degree. Adjacent edges may share a feasible color.

Simple forests have exact index b for b>=1. Multigraphs with forest
support, with arbitrary finite parallel multiplicity, admit 2B-1 colors
from supplied feasible local B-bin packings. Taking B=b is existential;
efficient computation of optimal bin packings is not claimed.

A cycle-breaking matching gives B+1 colors for simple cacti, including
non-bipartite ones. If b=1, one color suffices. The retained bipartite
unicyclic family proves the exact worst-case value b+1 for every b>=2.
A separate parallel forest-support family has exact index b+1 for every
b>=2; it attains 2b-1 only at b=2, not at all b.

The complete eleven-edge b=3 construction has exact index four. Its
specified frozen optimal root packing requires five colors to extend,
while recoloring gives four. This is a local-method obstruction, not a
counterexample to the Chung–Ross five-color target for b=3.

Empty graphs have index zero. Nonempty all-zero graphs use one color
under the convention that every edge is assigned. Disconnected components
reuse a palette, isolated vertices impose no constraint, and supplied
packings need not be optimal. All proof steps, parameterized construction
formulas and the full frozen construction are retained.

## Historical verification and reproduction boundary

The independent audit accepted the restricted results without a
substantive proof correction. It verified all seven central graph
instances, all 224 stored rejection assignments, 10,976 support-path
colorings on 2,744 graphs, 2,187 fixed-shape cactus weight-grid colorings,
and 59,377 rooted matching checks on the 10,026 cacti among all 33,868
labeled simple graphs through six vertices. The structural grid used
unit weights; it was not an exhaustive weighted grid on all those shapes.
Separate cross-checks covered 210 local-weight multisets and 1,536 palette
decisions. Nineteen semantic negative controls and edge-case controls
passed under normal Python, -O and -OO with identical substantive results.
Candidate programs were neither imported nor executed by the auditor.

The original generator's merge-event count was not reproduced because
it depends on local-packing tie-breaking. Independent graph/root counts,
feasibility, invariants and mathematical certificate conclusions agreed.
The counter is not a mathematical certificate or acceptance dependency.

The seven central graphs are specified mathematically by the retained
families and frozen example. Raw assignment tables, detailed graph and
load records, certificate packages, generated grid/control realizations,
code, copied source documents and images are excluded. The omitted
computational realizations cannot all be reconstructed from this edition
alone. It is not a complete computational reproduction package. Historical
checks support the written proofs and establish no unrestricted quantifier.
Preparation performed editorial and byte-integrity checks only, with no
new mathematical runs or scholarly-source retrieval/inspection.

## Sources and precise limits

Khan and Singh, [*On Weighted Bipartite Edge Coloring*](https://drops.dagstuhl.de/entities/document/10.4230/LIPIcs.FSTTCS.2015.136)
(FSTTCS 2015), states the exact bin-packing target and general asymptotic
20b/9+o(b) progress. Feige and Singh,
[*Edge Coloring and Decompositions of Weighted Graphs*](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/wp-content/uploads/2008/09/edgecoloring.pdf)
(2008), distinguishes bin-count and weighted-degree formulations.

Sannyasi, [*Improved Approximation Algorithms for Weighted Edge Coloring
of Graphs*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2012.15056v1), was directly inspected for
Theorems 10 and 11: b+1 for simple edge-disjoint-cycle graphs and
1.693b+12 for multigraph trees. No full-paper proof audit is claimed.

Huc, [*Weighted-Edge-Coloring of k-degenerate Graphs and Bin-Packing*](https://doi.org/10.1142/S0219265911002861)
(2011), has an [indexed abstract](https://sonar.ch/global/documents/62885)
with the formula missing and a total-weight parameter in prose. Primary
publisher access returned HTTP 403. Its exact theorem and proof remain
UNVERIFIED. No denied origin was bypassed. No precise Huc theorem is
imported, and no result is claimed novel. SOURCES.json records public
URLs, retained PDF hashes/sizes and the exact historical inspection limits.

The unrestricted Chung–Ross target remains unresolved by this work.
No novelty, priority, comprehensive literature or current-openness claim
is made. This AI-assisted manuscript is unrefereed. Acceptance means an
independent internal AI audit, not external human peer review, journal
acceptance or formal proof-assistant certification.

files are added under unsolved_math_prioritization/attempts/3000088.
QUEUE.md and unrelated paths are unchanged. Private coordination and
private personal data are excluded.

p1203.title: 30006523: Schubert-support skew-sum theorem and shortcut audit
p1203.body:
## Accepted restricted results

For ordinary stable Grothendieck and Schubert polynomials, the skew-sum
factorization uses the same symmetric rectangular factor for both bases.
The Schubert support of a skew sum is exactly the embedded Cartesian
product of the factor supports, and is left-weak convex if and only if
both factors are. The complete polynomial proof, left-weak upper-ideal
and product-interval proof, skew-indecomposable minimal-counterexample
reduction, and parameterized Boolean family from 132 are retained.

The general Schubert-support left-weak convexity conjecture remains
unresolved by this work. No novelty or current-openness claim is made.

The authored example F=S1243-S1342+2 S2341 has the same convex support,
coefficient-sign pattern, unique lowest term, and right-descent restriction
as G1243, yet pi_3 F=S1234+S2314 has a missing interval middle. The full
direct polynomial calculation is included. F is not any Grothendieck
polynomial, so it refutes only a coefficient-blind induction shortcut.
The G2143 example is attributed to Weigandt, Example 1.4. The G13254
right-weak failure is solely a convention check.

## Independent audit and exact finite limits

The restricted results were accepted without a substantive proof
correction. The independent historical audit reconstructed all 873
expansions in S1-S6, matched 1,746 full recursive/pipe polynomials, and
passed all 873 left-convexity checks. Dual extraction and stability
cover only S1-S5: 15,017 dual comparisons and 306 polynomial embeddings.
Not every secondary candidate count was independently reproduced.
Normal, -O, and -OO passed. Equality is decoded substantive JSON equality
after removal of the optimization field, not literal full JSON or byte
identity. The universal theorem rests on its written proof.

This AI-assisted work is unrefereed. Acceptance means an independent
internal AI audit, not external human peer review, journal acceptance,
or formal proof-assistant certification.

## Distribution and reproduction boundary

The complete written universal proofs, definitions, and analytical
identities are retained. Raw expansion datasets, computational certificate
tables, executable code, copied source documents/images, private sources,
private personal data, and private coordination material are excluded.
The exhaustive finite checks cannot be reproduced from this edition alone.
The G13254 analytical expansion is retained, but its complete recursive
calculation and computational certificate are omitted; reconstruction
requires the stated recurrences. It is not a premise of the universal
theorem. The F and Boolean-family derivations are fully written out.

Editorial preparation performed byte-integrity and preservation checks
only, with no new mathematical execution or scholarly-source inspection.
The accepted original candidate and audit remain unchanged.

## Sources and status

Anna Weigandt, joint work with Judy (Hsin-Hui) Chiang,
[*On the Schubert Support of Grothendieck Polynomials*](https://doi.org/10.4171/owr/2026/2),
Oberwolfach Report 2/2026, printed pages 132-133, states the target in
left weak order. Its inverse-fireworks statement covers only the first
two conjectures, unlike its reported Grassmannian and 1 times dominant
cases. No independent proof of those source-reported cases is claimed.

Anna Weigandt, [*Changing Bases with Pipe Dream Combinatorics*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.07306v1),
supplies operator conventions, stability, the pipe formula, and G2143.
The retained v1 PDF's internal date is June 10, 2025; v1 submission was
June 8, 2025. Only the recursive sentence before (2.1) is identified as
having the reversed inequality; the displayed descent formulas and top
monomial fix the convention. No dynamically substituted HTML version
controls the mathematics.

The [Chiang research page](https://sites.google.com/view/judy-chiang/research)
was historically observed to list the project paper in progress. That
manuscript-status observation does not establish current openness or
novelty. SOURCES.json states retained-source hashes, sizes, and historical
retrieval and inspection limits.

Exactly eight authored proof/audit/acceptance/provenance/verification files
are added under unsolved_math_prioritization/attempts/30006523. QUEUE.md
and unrelated paths are unchanged.

p1204.title: 30004615: normal modular-freeness descent and reflection obstructions
p1204.body:
## Restricted result and exact limits

For even lattices of signature (n,2), n >= 3, polynomiality of the full integral-weight, trivial-character orthogonal modular-form ring descends from a finite-index normal subgroup to an overgroup generated by actual linear reflections. The complete equivariant-generator lemmas, affine Spec geometry, effective-action argument, and proof preserving the original modular weights are retained.

The normalizer extension is conditional: it stabilizes but need not reach the overgroup. The full order-12 matrix/ring example obstructs a general normal-core shortcut. The Wang--Williams-dependent parity example refutes the projective-reflection weakening only. Actual reflections, negative reflections, and projective actions are distinguished throughout. The general nonnormal conjecture remains unresolved by this work.

## Review and dependencies

The accepted mathematical proof and full independent logical audit are preserved without substantive correction. Baily--Borel, Chevalley--Shephard--Todd, Wang's optional reflection-generation result, and the specified Wang--Williams theorems remain named dependencies; their original proofs or underlying Fourier computations were not independently reproduced.

This AI-assisted work is unrefereed. Acceptance records an independent internal AI audit, not external human peer review, journal acceptance, or formal proof-assistant certification. No novelty, priority, complete-literature, or current-openness claim is made.

## Distribution and verification boundaries

This prose-only edition includes exactly eight authored files. The complete analytical matrices, all-degree invariant-ring presentations, parity formulas, and written proofs are retained. Executable code, raw datasets, detailed computational certificate tables, copied source bodies/images, and private coordination are excluded. This is not a computational reproduction package.

Historical independent finite checks cover ordinary degree 64 and modular weight 72, including 11,809 collision-free normal-form images, eight mathematical controls, and seven candidate byte controls. Their saved outputs are byte-identical under normal Python, -O, and -OO. They are supporting checks, not proofs of the modular theorem or all-degree presentations. p1205.title: 30004665: D4 counterexample to the canonical-potential exponent converse
p1205.body:

p1206.title: 3142: exact eight-color cyclic covers of the Clebsch graph
p1206.body:
## Accepted restricted result

For every positive integer t, the explicitly defined cyclic cover H_t is a finite, simple, connected, nonbipartite 5-regular graph on 16t vertices, and chi(H_t^(3/3)) = 8. The notation means the third power of the third subdivision; the fraction does not cancel. The original graph-coloring conjecture remains unresolved by this work.

## Complete proof and numerical certificate

The XOR base on four-bit vectors uses generators {1,2,4,8,15}. The complete 96-entry coloring table is retained unchanged, together with explicit incoming color sets and a proof of the exact terminal/arc constraints. The positive certificate is independently checkable by hand from these data.

The full locally injective pullback lemma and cyclic-cover construction are retained. Written arguments establish simplicity, local bijectivity, degree five, connectivity and nonbipartiteness for every positive t, including t=1 and t=2. A square K15 and the regular-graph incoming-color lemma exclude seven colors. The infinite conclusion does not rest on finite tests.

The singleton-incoming parameter equals 16 on the base and lies between 15 and 16 on every cover. This obstructs only that stronger restriction, while the unrestricted value eight satisfies the target eleven throughout the family. No exact singleton value is claimed for t>1; the two-incoming-color model is not ruled out.

## Full logical audit and historical finite scope

The complete six-part independent audit accepts the restricted theorem without mathematical correction. Its separately written Boolean-reachability checker did not read candidate programs as source, import them, or execute them. Historical runs cover t=1,...,17 and t=31: 12,644,736 unordered subdivision pairs and 132,480 power edges per coloring, for both the eight-color and sixteen-color constructions in each execution mode. The distance-criterion cross-check also covers all 1,099 labeled simple graphs of orders one through five, totaling 115,851 subdivision pairs. Thirteen incorrect controls are rejected per mode. Saved normal, -O and -OO audit outputs are byte-identical.

Candidate checks are separately identified and cover t=1,...,16. Failed or incomplete searches establish no lower bound. Editorial preparation authenticates saved metadata and document bytes; it does not rerun historical mathematical programs or retrieve or inspect additional scholarly sources.

This is not an executable computational reproduction package. The full table and proofs are provided; raw exhaustive computation records, raw search outputs and code are omitted. Thus the positive certificate can be independently checked, while this edition does not supply an executable replay of the historical exhaustive checks.

## Prior negative resolution and attribution

Record the complete reconstructed counterexample and mathematical audit for 30000663 / OWR-1452-027. p1262.title: 30001248: credited sharp triangle modulus threshold and full audit
p1262.body:
# Sharp modulus range for triangle counts in dense random graphs

For fixed p in (0,1), ordinary triangles T_n counted once in G(n,p), and every positive integer sequence q_n, max over all residues a of |q_n P(T_n = a mod q_n)-1| tends to zero if and only if q_n=o(n^2). This includes q=1, bounded, composite, oscillating, arbitrarily slowly subcritical, critical and supercritical sequences. Triangle standard-deviation normalization starts at n>=3; the known ordinary 2K2 supplement starts at n>=4.

p1270.title: [2200014] Credited disproof of Shapiro's weighted parity conjecture
p1270.body:
## Credited negative resolution

Publishes the proof reconstruction, mathematical audit, scoped acceptance, and public verification metadata for **2200014 / AMR-021-0014**, Conjecture 9 in Shapiro's polynomial problem list.

The conjecture is false. **Katkova, Shapiro and Vishnyakova (2024)** are credited for the disproof and primitive family in [In search of Newton-type inequalities, Section 5](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2403.12200v1#page=20). Their work was published in *Journal of Mathematical Analysis and Applications* 538(1), article 128349, [DOI 10.1016/j.jmaa.2024.128349](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jmaa.2024.128349).

Our exact degree-24 reconstruction is
`R(x) = (38x^2 - 188x + 326) product_{j=1}^{22}(10^6 x + 10^6 + j)`.
It has strictly positive integer coefficients and exactly **22 distinct simple negative real roots**, while the selected weighted-index parity sequence has **at most 20 changes**. This disproves the bound both for distinct roots and for roots counted with multiplicity.

## Exact scope and proof

For a real polynomial of actual degree n with every coefficient strictly positive, the statistic is `c_k = (k+1)a_k^2 - k a_{k-1}a_{k+1}`, with the two auxiliary endpoint coefficients zero. Only strictly positive c_k are retained, in increasing index order; the count is of consecutive parity changes, with no cyclic closing comparison.

The full self-contained symbolic proof includes the compact coefficient formula, explicit uniform relative perturbation bound below 1/2000, robust weighted-sign inequalities, parity-subsequence argument, and complete root factorization. No omitted arithmetic program, table, or numeric certificate is needed. The audit's exact parity equality of 20 and complete sign pattern are supplemental finite cross-checks; the sufficient symbolic bound already proves the counterexample.

[Shapiro's original Conjecture 9](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1503.05295v1#page=4) is credited there to Forsgård and Shapiro. No novelty, construction-priority, or minimum-degree claim is made.

The finite-product endpoint correction applies **only to the inspected arXiv:2403.12200v1**. The publisher PDF was not inspected. The corrected finite formulas have the same limiting values, and the self-contained proof does not depend on the misindexed products.

p1274.title: 2307072: audited Beurling annihilator witnesses
p1274.body:
# Explicit Beurling-transform counterexamples in an analytic annihilator

Both endpoint questions in the bilinear analytic annihilator of Hayman and Lingham, Problem 7.72, have negative answers under the printed negative-kernel convention. The norm-one input v(z)=z/bar(z) on the unit disc annihilates every integrable analytic test function, while its Beurling transform is 1+log|z|^2 and is essentially unbounded. Explicit polynomials v_m(z)=z^2 sum_{j=0}^{m-1}(1-|z|^2)^j lie in the same annihilator, have norm one and have transform norm H_m, the m-th harmonic number. Each fixed polynomial has bounded transform, but no common uniform constant exists.

This is an exposition and independent explicit verification of consequences of classical formulas, with a self-contained proof. Iwaniec published the exact nonpolynomial witness, output and primitive in 1986. Gill published the general positive-angular transform formula in 2010; the polynomial formula and harmonic-number norm follow by elementary specialization. The 2019 Hayman-Lingham book attributes resolution of Problem 7.72 to Volberg. Its cited reference 52 is the 2008 Banuelos-Janakiraman finite-p paper; the current audit did not locate an explicit full-target account there or a separate Volberg proof. This limitation does not refute the book attribution. No new solution, witness, transform mechanism, first polynomial construction, first harmonic-number calculation or current worldwide openness is claimed. Priority for an earlier explicit combined statement in the exact annihilator notation remains unestablished.

p1292.title: 30001617: audited prior counterexample to unrestricted dyadic tail LIL
p1292.body:
## Result and attribution

Problem 30001617 (OWR-4531-020): the unrestricted dyadic tail LIL assertion has a negative answer. This packet gives a complete, self-contained construction of a real L2 function on [0,1) with total realized square function at most one, strictly positive square tails Q_n tending to zero, and

    limsup |f - f_n| / sqrt(Q_n log log(1/Q_n)) = infinity

almost everywhere. Zero extension gives a globally integrable real-line counterexample to Artur Nicolau's question in Oberwolfach Report 49/2010, printed p. 2872.

This negative phenomenon is prior work of Santosh Ghimire, presented in 2011 and developed in his 2012 dissertation, Section 3.3. The proof is an all-positive stopped-block reconstruction, with complete L2 and almost-sure convergence, terminal conditional-mean identification, and a summable future-error budget. Successful-block start indices are used pathwise and are not asserted to be stopping times.

The cited positive theorems assume a uniform within-atom square-tail comparison. The construction directly violates that hypothesis. Selected-time conclusions do not bound the unrestricted full limsup, and no specialized positive LIL theorem is imported or certified.

p1298.title: 30001058: sharp dimension-two dilation thresholds with full conditional scope

For problem 30001058, the full original OWR Theorem 2 package, including its conditional strict alternation, and the actual lattice-polygon package have exactly the positive-integer feasible pairs
